memory_candidates.content: When adding a reverse-direction 'deployed but no longer declared' detector on top of an additive-only declarative deploy engine (loader.copy_category driven by CATEGORY_DESCRIPTORS/list_key), reuse the existing declared-side enumeration (walk_category_leaves) rather than re-deriving a second path-mapping table -- but explicitly skip any category with target_is_project_root=true (e.g. a 'data' category): calling the same leaf-walker on it will nil-concat on a missing target_subdir since its target is outside the tree being walked. A category descriptor table is not automatically loop-safe for every consumer just because it was designed for the copy engine's own use.

Before treating a scratch-tree clean-regenerate diff as ground truth for 'live-only == orphan', classify every live-only line into a named exclusion class first (runtime artifacts like tmp/*, RESUME.md, __pycache__/*.pyc, and any runtime-provisioned tool env such as a Python venv under a declared provisioning script's own directory; merged/generated artifacts assembled from multiple sources like CLAUDE.md/settings.json/context/index.json; .syncprotect-protected paths, which a from-scratch clone never receives at all, not just 'never overwritten'). Skipping this classification step produces false-positive orphan counts that can be off by 10x (in this task: 4 real orphans vs. an unclassified diff dominated by a ~4700-file provisioned virtualenv).
